description: Create or update custom field definitions by (entity, fieldName) — max 100 per call, case-insensitive match. Check for a built-in first: a custom field is plain data that reorder recommendations, purchasing, pricing, reports and fulfillment never read. Each create names a purpose and a purposeDetail (the user's reason, saved on the field). On an item, a purpose a built-in covers (reorder policy, supplier, category/brand/group, lifecycle, pricing, barcode, tracking, units, dimensions, location, components, tags, notes) is not created: the row comes back needs_review with builtInAlternatives. Show those to the user, and create the field only if they still want it, by resending the row with builtInReviewed=true. fieldName is the upsert identity and never changes once set; omit it on create to derive it from name (snake_case, matching the key the Spark app generates — an all-symbol name fails validation). A supplied fieldName must follow the same convention: lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, starting with a letter or digit. name and type are required when creating; type is IMMUTABLE on update (create a new field instead) and calculated fields cannot be authored here (web app only). Every other property is preserve-on-omit. Options for list/multilist fields are matched by supplied id first, then case-insensitive name — matched options keep their id (and every stored value pointing at it), new names get a generated id, and omitted existing options are REMOVED. itemGroupIds and isCostAttribute only apply to the item entity. validateOnly=true dry-runs every row. Partial success with per-row errors; resubmitting converges. Requires an operator (unpinned) credential — field definitions are tenant-wide schema.

customFields.description: Custom-field definition rows to create/update (max 100). entity is required per row; name, type, purpose and purposeDetail are required when creating.

builtInReviewed.description: Set true only after the user has seen the built-in feature a challenged create pointed to and still wants a custom field. Ignored on update.

entity.description: Target entity: item, member, businessPartner, warehouse, or workOrder. Required; part of the upsert identity.

fieldName.description: Storage key / upsert identity within the entity (case-insensitive). Omit on create to derive it from name in snake_case — the exact key the Spark app generates for that display name ("Country of Origin (ISO-2)" -> "country_of_origin_iso_2"), so an MCP-created field and an app-created one converge instead of colliding. A supplied value must follow the same convention: lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, starting with a letter or digit. Never changes an existing field's key.

isCostAttribute.description: item-entity only: offer this field as a price-book cost driver. Preserve-on-omit.

isImportIdentifier.description: When true, imports may resolve records by this field's value. Preserve-on-omit.

itemGroupIds.description: item-entity only: item-group ids (GUIDs) this field is limited to. Empty list clears the limitation. Preserve-on-omit when null.

name.description: Display name. Required when creating; preserve-on-omit on update. Unique per entity.

options.description: Options for list/multilist fields. Existing options are matched by name (case-insensitive) so their ids — and stored values pointing at them — survive; new names get new ids; omitted existing options are REMOVED. Preserve-on-omit when null.

id.description: Option id — omit for new options (an id is generated). Supplying the id of an existing option renames it.

purpose.description: What the field is for. Required when creating; ignored on update. One of: reorder (reorder point, min/max, safety stock, lead time), supplier (default supplier, vendor minimum order quantity), classification (category, brand, item group, product line, department), lifecycle (active, discontinued, phase-out), pricing (cost, price, customer or tier prices, volume breaks), identifier (barcode/UPC, trading-partner item code), tracking (lot, serial or expiry tracking), units (unit of measure, case pack, unit conversions), dimensions (length, width, height, weight, volume), location (bin, shelf, preferred pick location), components (kit, bundle, bill of materials), tags (free-form labels), notes (description or internal notes), spec (a product specification or price-book cost driver, e.g. binding or trim size), other (none of these). On an item, every purpose except spec and other matches a built-in Spark feature: the first create is answered with that feature instead of a field, for you to review with the user.

purposeDetail.description: Required when creating: in a sentence, what the user wants this field to do, in their own terms (10-500 characters). Saved on the field. When builtInReviewed is true, also say why the built-in feature does not fit.

type.description: Field type: decimal, text, boolean, list, multilist, or date. Required when creating; IMMUTABLE on update (create a new field instead). date values are written as ISO yyyy-MM-dd strings. calculated fields can only be authored in the Spark app.

validateOnly.description: true = dry-run: validate + probe every row and report the would-be action per row, writing nothing.

name: upsert_custom_fields
title: Upsert Custom Fields
